But the gridlock really has just started in the last few years, honestly. I went back and looked at the original rules of the Senate. There were six pages, 51% ruled a day. They had a filibuster rule then that, but it was a physical filibuster rule. It wasn't even used until the 1850s. It was abused in the 1890s. Then in 1913, the Senate got together and said, well, and that was a year they changed from being appointed in the Senate to being elected in the Senate. So that's what they did. They put a 67 vote rule, a 67% vote rule. Then in 76, they said, well, it's still not working. We'll reduce that to 60 votes. And today, if the minority party decides to shut down the functionality of the Senate, they can do that. And that's what's happened under Harry Reid, and that's what's happening right now, in my opinion. And Republicans do it, too, when they're in the minority.
